# Ultiproxy

> Agent-First Universal LLM Subscription Proxy (:9050)
> Pooling GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, Claude, Antigravity, Grok, DeepSeek, Z.ai, and local vLLM into a single unified endpoint.

Ultiproxy is an ultra-fast, local-first proxy daemon that multiplexes multiple upstream AI subscriptions into unified OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs. It provides live per-provider quota monitoring, per-API-key accounting, zero-marginal-cost pooling, and a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for autonomous agents.

## Key Capabilities

- **Unified Surface**: Exposes `POST /v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI format) and `POST /v1/messages` (Anthropic format) on port `9050`.
- **Zero-Marginal-Cost Subscription Pooling**: Combines flat-fee developer subscriptions into a unified high-capacity gateway, bypassing per-token API billing.
- **Quota Monitoring**: Live per-provider quota windows and credit state via the MCP `get_quota_status` tool, `/api/quota`, and `quota.txt` — operators decide routing; the proxy never reroutes on quota by itself.
- **Embedded MCP Server**: Streamable HTTP and SSE Model Context Protocol endpoints allow agents to introspect active models, check remaining quota, and toggle backends dynamically.
- **Per-API-Key Accounting**: Granular tracking and attribution of prompt tokens, completion tokens, cached tokens, and request counts per client.
- **Quota Dashboard API**: Serves unified JSON subscription health, reset windows, and quota gauges at `/api/quota`.
- **Reasoning & Tool Streaming**: Transparently preserves reasoning tokens (`reasoning_content` / thinking blocks), function/tool calls, and vision inputs.

---

## API Endpoints Reference

Complete OpenAPI 3.1 specification is available in `docs/openapi.yaml`.

### 1. OpenAI Chat Completions
- **Route**: `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- **Auth**: `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` (an `x-api-key: <api-key>` header is accepted on every route as well)
- **Description**: Standard OpenAI chat completions endpoint supporting text, multi-turn dialogue, tool calls, image payloads, and streaming SSE.
- **Supported Parameters**:
  - `model` (string, required): Model ID (e.g., `gpt-4o`, `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `deepseek-r1`, `copilot/gpt-4o`)
  - `messages` (array, required): Conversation turns with `role` (`system`, `user`, `assistant`, `tool`), `content`, and optional `tool_calls`
  - `stream` (boolean): When true, streams Server-Sent Events (`data: {"choices": [{"delta": ...}]}`)
  - `tools` (array): List of OpenAI function definitions
  - `tool_choice` (string | object): Tool execution policy
  - `temperature` (number): Sampling temperature (0.0 to 2.0)
  - `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` (integer): Output limit
- **Sample Request**:
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:9050/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-up-local-agent-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4o",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Ping"}],
    "stream": false
  }'
```

### 2. Anthropic Messages Protocol
- **Route**: `POST /v1/messages`
- **Auth**: `x-api-key: <api-key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`
- **Description**: Direct Anthropic Messages API compatibility for Claude Code, Hermes, and Anthropic clients.
- **Supported Parameters**:
  - `model` (string, required): e.g. `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`, `anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet`
  - `messages` (array, required): List of input message objects (`role`, `content`)
  - `max_tokens` (integer, required): Maximum tokens to generate
  - `system` (string | array): System prompt instructions
  - `stream` (boolean): Stream events (`content_block_start`, `content_block_delta`, etc.)
  - `tools` (array): Anthropic tool definitions
- **Sample Request**:
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:9050/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: sk-up-local-agent-key" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
    "max_tokens": 1024,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain zero-marginal-cost proxying."}]
  }'
```

### 3. Model Catalog
- **Route**: `GET /v1/models`
- **Auth**: `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`
- **Description**: Enumerates only ids a client can put in `"model"`: catalog aliases (config + MCP `set_model_alias`), one entry per discovered upstream model on OpenAI-compatible lanes (model discovery is ON by default; `model_list_passthrough:false` opts out; the `anthropic` lane discovers its own list from `GET /v1/models` with the `anthropic-version` header) exposed as `<lane>/<model>` -- the exact id routing accepts -- and one `<lane>/<default>` entry for lanes that have a real default model (e.g. `antigravity/gemini-3.7-flash-high`), which keeps non-discoverable lanes advertised. Bare lane names are NOT listed: a lane name is a routing prefix, not a model; `"model": "<lane>"` (no slash) still routes only as a legacy form. A lane with an empty discovery cache and no default model lists nothing. Test lanes (`probe`, `fake`, ...) are dropped when `ULTIPROXY_HIDE_TEST_LANES=1`. Discovery runs when a lane is registered, again at startup for lanes whose cache is still empty, and every 6h afterwards; listing itself is served from that cache and never fans out to the upstreams. Each row advertises the metadata a source actually reported: the context window under both names (`context_length` and `max_model_len` carry the same integer), the output cap (`max_output_tokens`), and modalities (`architecture.input_modalities` / `architecture.output_modalities`, plus `supports_vision: true` exactly when image is an input). Precedence, per field: operator alias (`context_limit`, `max_output`, `input_modalities` / `output_modalities`) > live discovery > cited static catalog (`pkg/modelmeta`, extended with `data_dir/windows.json` -- every catalog row cites the vendor doc URL it came from) > the key is omitted. Unknown is omitted, never `0`, `false` or `[]`, and the ambiguous legacy `max_tokens` is never emitted. Windows are read from every upstream dialect: `max_model_len`, `context_length`, `top_provider.context_length`, `meta.context_length`, `meta.n_ctx` (served, preferred over `meta.n_ctx_train`), `context_window`, and Anthropic `max_input_tokens`; output caps from `top_provider.max_completion_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and Anthropic `max_tokens`; modalities from `architecture.input_modalities` / `output_modalities`, top-level modality arrays, `architecture.modality` (`"text+image->text"`) or `supports_vision`, normalized to `text|image|file|audio|video` (`pdf` -> `file`). Nothing is inferred from a model name and no lane capability is copied onto a listed id. `context_length` is advisory metadata; `max_output_tokens` is enforced (the request's `max_tokens` is clamped to it).
- **Response Structure**:
```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "copilot/claude-3-5-sonnet",
      "object": "model",
      "created": 1729600000,
      "owned_by": "github-copilot",
      "context_length": 200000,
      "max_model_len": 200000,
      "max_output_tokens": 8192,
      "architecture": { "input_modalities": ["text", "image"], "output_modalities": ["text"] },
      "supports_vision": true,
      "benchmarks": { "swe_bench": 49.2, "humaneval": 92.4 },
      "provider": { "id": "copilot", "status": "ok" }
    },
    {
      "id": "openai/gpt-4o",
      "object": "model",
      "created": 1715560000,
      "owned_by": "openai",
      "context_length": 128000,
      "max_output_tokens": 4096,
      "benchmarks": { "swe_bench": 38.8, "humaneval": 90.2 },
      "provider": { "id": "openai", "status": "ok" }
    }
  ]
}
```

### 4. Quota Dashboard API
- **Route**: `GET /api/quota`
- **Auth**: Bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` or `x-api-key: <api-key>`) whenever client keys or an admin key are configured; the daemon serves it unauthenticated only when no keys are configured at all, like every other route.
- **Description**: Returns live subscription health, reset windows, and quota gauges across all 12 providers.
- **Contract Schema**:
```json
{
  "providers": [
    {
      "id": "copilot",
      "name": "GitHub Copilot",
      "plan": "Pro (annual)",
      "status": "ok",
      "gauge_pct": 34.0,
      "windows": [
        {
          "label": "Premium requests",
          "used_pct": 34.0,
          "reset_at": "2026-09-03T18:00:00Z",
          "seconds_remaining": 7200
        }
      ],
      "bars": [
        {
          "label": "Premium requests",
          "used": 340,
          "limit": 1000,
          "remaining": 660,
          "unit": "requests",
          "pct": 34.0
        }
      ],
      "updated": "2026-09-03T16:00:00Z",
      "detail": "Premium 66% remaining · resets in 2h"
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total": 12,
    "ok": 11,
    "unavailable": 1,
    "next_reset": {
      "seconds": 1800,
      "provider": "OpenAI Codex",
      "reset_at": "2026-09-03T16:30:00Z"
    },
    "fetched_at": "16:00:00",
    "fetched_at_epoch": 1788440000,
    "stale": false,
    "age_seconds": 2,
    "refreshing": false,
    "refresh_started_at": null,
    "refresh_min_interval": 30,
    "last_refresh_error": null
  }
}
```

### 5. Accounting & Stats Endpoints
- **Route**: `GET /api/stats/summary`
  - **Auth**: same as every other route (Bearer or `x-api-key` when keys are configured).
  - Aggregated prompt, completion, and cached tokens, request count, distinct active client keys, and a `provider_breakdown` map of `{requests, tokens, errors}` per lane.
  - `estimated_cost_saved_usd` is the pay-as-you-go equivalent of the recorded traffic (the sum of the alias-priced usage cost): the pooled subscriptions are flat fee, so that is what the same tokens would have cost on a metered API. `total_tokens` / `total_cost` are the older names for the same totals and are kept for compatibility.
  - Numbers come from the daemon's SQLite telemetry store; a daemon built without storage answers the same shape with zeros.
- **Route**: `GET /api/stats/by-client`
  - **Auth**: same as every other route.
  - `?window=1h|24h|7d|30d` (default `7d`); an unparseable window is a 400.
  - Returns an array of per-client records ordered by request count, descending: `client_id`, `client_name`, `client_key_hash`, `request_count`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `cost`, `error_count`, `rate_limited_count`, `last_active`.
  - `client_id` is the configured client key name when the recorded digest is known, the digest itself when it is not, and `anonymous` for rows recorded without a key.
  - Enables team quota isolation and agent auditability.

### 6. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Endpoints
- **Streamable HTTP MCP**: `GET /mcp` and `POST /mcp`
- **Legacy SSE MCP**: `GET /mcp/sse`
- **Protocol**: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP/SSE.
- **Exposed Agent Tools** (each one carries a full self-describing docstring through `tools/list`):
  - `list_models`: Client-visible model ids with their provider lane, enabled state, context limit, max output, pricing tag, benchmark scores and source (`alias`, `discovery` for `<lane>/<model>`, `default` for `<lane>/<default>`). Advertises the same id set as `GET /v1/models`, so the two surfaces cannot drift; ids disabled with `toggle_model` stay listed with `enabled: false` so they can be switched back on.
  - `get_quota_status`: Remaining allocations, units, and seconds until reset for one provider lane (antigravity, xai, copilot, codex, freebuff, zai, or a runtime lane). Monitoring only - the proxy never auto-reroutes on quota. Lanes with no quota surface answer "has no quota mechanism"; a lane that is not logged in (e.g. codex) answers with a snapshot whose `detail` says to start a login with the `initiate_oauth_login` MCP tool.
  - `toggle_model`: Enables or disables a model id at runtime without deleting its alias mapping.
  - `get_client_usage`: Token accounting (prompt, completion, cached) plus request counts for one client key or overall, over a window such as `1h`, `24h`, `7d`.
  - `initiate_oauth_login`: Starts a non-blocking OAuth login for subscription lanes; returns the sign-in URL and the device-flow `user_code`. Logged-in credentials are refreshed automatically: a background refresher renews any lane credential with under 10 minutes of life left every 5 minutes (no inbound request needed), and an upstream 401/403 invalidates the credential, refreshes it and retries the request exactly once before the first byte. Refresh logs carry the lane name and the new expiry only, never a token.
  - `check_oauth_login`: Polls a pending device-flow login (e.g. xai) or completes a server-side token exchange.
  - `submit_oauth_code`: Submits the authorization code from the redirect callback URL (e.g. antigravity).
  - `list_model_aliases` / `set_model_alias` / `remove_model_alias`: The alias table (client-visible name -> provider lane + upstream id, with `context_limit`, `max_output`, `pricing_tag`, `input_cost`, `output_cost`); runtime changes persist in `data_dir/aliases.json`.
  - `get_provider_timeouts` / `set_provider_timeout` / `remove_provider_timeout`: Per-lane timeouts as Go duration strings (`10m`, `3m30s`), persisted in `data_dir/timeouts.json`.
  - `add_provider` / `remove_provider` / `list_providers`: Runtime lane registration (OpenAI-compatible lanes via name/base_url/api_key/quirks, plus the antigravity, anthropic, codex and freebuff custom-wire kinds), persisted in `data_dir/providers.json`; `list_providers` redacts secrets. `add_provider` runs model discovery before replying and reports "discovered N models". OAuth lanes (e.g. xai) must be added with `quirks: {"auth_via_oauth_manager": true}` and an empty `api_key`, otherwise the lane carries a static key and no code path can refresh it.
  - `refresh_models`: Re-fetches `GET <base>/v1/models` and caches the ids so `<lane>/<model>` appears in `/v1/models`. Manual override on top of the automatic schedule (registration, startup backfill, 6h refresh).

### 7. Discovery & Health
- **Route**: `GET /llms.txt` — Machine-readable overview for LLMs. The document is served from `llms.txt` in the process working directory when present, and otherwise from the copy embedded in the binary at build time (`go:embed`, see `llms_embed.go`), so an installed daemon serves it with no source checkout present.
- **Route**: `GET /healthz` — Service health and upstream connectivity status.

---

## Installation Guide

### Fast Install (Linux & macOS)

Install the precompiled binary to `~/.local/bin`; it is immediately runnable with zero configuration:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ultiproxy.dev/install.sh | bash
```

To review operations prior to execution:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://ultiproxy.dev/install.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run
```

### Systemd User Service Setup

The installer automatically configures a hardened systemd user unit on Linux systems.

Manage the daemon via `systemctl --user`:
```bash
# Start and enable Ultiproxy on login
systemctl --user enable --now ultiproxy

# View daemon logs
journalctl --user -u ultiproxy -f

# Check status
systemctl --user status ultiproxy
```

---

## Configuration Reference

Ultiproxy is zero-config on startup. `ultiproxy serve` (optionally `ULTIPROXY_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9050 ultiproxy serve` to bind a remote interface, or `--data-dir` to place persistent state) starts the daemon with no providers, no aliases and no timeouts defined; nothing has to exist before the first request. There is no config file to read or write, and no administration CLI either: the daemon binary only serves (its only flags are `--config` and `--data-dir`, plus a `version` subcommand), so MCP is the sole control plane.

ALL configuration is applied dynamically, at runtime, by agents or operators over MCP (`POST /mcp`, legacy SSE on `/mcp/sse`):

- `add_provider` / `remove_provider` / `list_providers` - provider lanes
- `set_model_alias` / `remove_model_alias` / `list_model_aliases` - client-visible model names
- `set_provider_timeout` / `remove_provider_timeout` / `get_provider_timeouts` - per-lane timeouts
- `initiate_oauth_login` / `check_oauth_login` / `submit_oauth_code` - subscription logins
- `list_models` / `toggle_model` / `get_quota_status` / `get_client_usage` / `refresh_models` - inspection and soft switches

Changes take effect immediately (no restart) and persist in the daemon's `data_dir`, which is restored on the next start: `providers.json` (registered lanes), `aliases.json` (model aliases), `timeouts.json` (per-lane timeouts), plus `credentials/` for OAuth token state and the SQLite telemetry database.

Client keys are optional: declaring them turns on Bearer authentication and per-key attribution; with none declared every request is accepted, which suits a localhost-only daemon. `ULTIPROXY_ADDR` is the only environment switch needed for a remote bind.

---

## Client Integration Examples

### 1. OpenCode Configuration
Add Ultiproxy to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "ultiproxy": {
      "name": "Ultiproxy Universal Gateway",
      "type": "openai",
      "baseURL": "http://localhost:9050/v1",
      "apiKey": "sk-up-local-agent-key",
      "models": [
        "gpt-4o",
        "claude-3-5-sonnet",
        "deepseek-r1",
        "copilot/claude-3-5-sonnet"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### 2. Hermes Agent Configuration
Configure Hermes custom provider in your agent's config YAML:

```yaml
llm:
  provider: "custom"
  base_url: "http://localhost:9050/v1"
  api_key: "sk-up-local-agent-key"
  model: "claude-3-5-sonnet"
  max_tokens: 8192
  temperature: 0.2
  extra_headers:
    X-Client-Id: "hermes-agent-primary"
```

### 3. Claude Code Integration
Point Claude Code to the Anthropic compatibility endpoint using environment variables:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:9050"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="sk-up-local-agent-key"

# Run Claude Code directly against pooled subscriptions
claude
```

### 4. Cursor / OpenAI SDK
For any tool expecting OpenAI endpoints:

```typescript
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "http://localhost:9050/v1",
  apiKey: "sk-up-local-agent-key",
});

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-4o",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Optimize this algorithm." }],
  stream: true,
});
```

## Supported Providers & Subscriptions

| Provider | Supported Subscription | Default Models |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GitHub Copilot** | Pro, Business, Enterprise | `gpt-4o`, `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `o1-preview` |
| **Google Antigravity** | Gemini Advanced / Vertex | `gemini-1.5-pro`, `gemini-1.5-flash` |
| **OpenAI Codex / Plus** | ChatGPT Plus, Team, Enterprise | `gpt-4o`, `o1-preview`, `o1-mini` |
| **Anthropic** | Claude Pro, Console Team | `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `claude-3-opus`, `haiku` |
| **xAI Grok** | X Premium+, xAI Console | `grok-2`, `grok-beta` |
| **DeepSeek** | DeepSeek Balance / VIP | `deepseek-v3`, `deepseek-r1` |
| **Z.ai Coding Plan** | Z.ai Subscription | `glm-4`, `deepseek-coder` |
| **Augure AI** | Augure Pro | `augure-code-v1` |
| **OpenRouter** | OpenRouter Tier credits | Fallback gateway across 200+ models |
| **Freebuff** | Freebuff Account | Mirror inference endpoints |
| **OpenCode Go** | OpenCode Subscription | Coding optimized pipeline |
| **Local vLLM** | None (Local GPU / CPU inference) | `llama-3.1-70b`, `qwen-2.5-coder` |

---

## Security Model

1. **Localhost Isolation**: By default, Ultiproxy binds strictly to `127.0.0.1:9050`.
2. **Token Encapsulation**: Upstream subscription keys and OAuth refresh tokens stay inside the daemon's `data_dir` credential store (never returned by any MCP tool, never forwarded to downstream clients).
3. **Bearer Token Validation**: Inbound agent and developer connections require a configured client API key (`sk-up-...`).
4. **Per-Key Rate Limits**: Granular accounting prevents runaway agent loops from consuming pooled upstream quotas.
